 Odisha govt evacuates nearly 50,000 people as Cyclone 'Akvan' shifts course towards state 
 Odisha's Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reported evacuating about 50,000 people ahead of cyclone 'Akvan'. The state government aims for zero casualties during the evacuation efforts in various districts. PTI 
 Published On Nov 19, 2026 at 11:56 AM IST

 Odisha chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said around 50,000 people have so far been evacuated to safety ahead of the likely landfall of severe cyclonic storm 'Akvan' between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern state. Majhi, who presided over a high-level review meeting on the preparedness of the state government on Wednesday, said the highest number of people will be evacuated from Ganjam district and the process was underway. "Our target is zero casualties, and the evacuation drive has been launched in a massive manner, both in the plains and hilly terrain," he said. People were being shifted to safer locations from several villages of Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts, the CM said. The state government has set up 3,000 cyclone shelters, of which 448 were already operational, Majhi said. Odisha has allocated ₹20 crore to 15 districts to carry out relief and rescue operations. Majhi said the IMD has issued a warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in 11 districts for Thursday and Friday - Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda. The average wind speed along the Odisha coast would be around 100 kmph, he said. The Odisha government has also announced the closure of schools in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal districts for three days from Thursday, suspended leaves of employees, and deployed senior bureaucrats in vulnerable areas in the wake of the approaching cyclone.
